style: Say slowly and clearly, like a friendly teacher helping young English learners learn community words
lines: Welcome to our town! Tap a place to visit.
Teachers work here. They help children learn.
I want to learn to read.
A teacher works at the school.
Librarians work here. They help you find books.
I need a book about dinosaurs.
A librarian works at the library.
Firefighters work here. They put out fires and keep people safe.
I want to learn about fire safety.
I go to the fire station.
A firefighter works at the fire station.
Firefighters put out fires and keep people safe.
Doctors and nurses work here. They help sick and hurt people get better.
I hurt my arm and need a doctor.
A doctor works at the hospital.
Doctors and nurses help sick and hurt people get better.
Police officers work here. They keep the community safe.
I am lost and need help.
I go to the police station.
A police officer works at the police station.
Police officers keep the community safe.
Mail carriers work here. They bring letters and packages.
I want to mail a letter to Grandma.
I go to the post office.
A mail carrier works at the post office.
Mail carriers bring letters and packages.
Cashiers work here. They help you pay for food.
I go to the grocery store.
A cashier works at the grocery store.
Cashiers help you pay for food.
Bakers work here. They bake bread and cakes.
I want to buy a birthday cake.
A baker works at the bakery.
Park rangers work here. They take care of parks and nature.
I want to play on the swings.
A park ranger works at the park.
Park rangers take care of parks and nature.
Veterinarians work here. They help sick animals.
A veterinarian works at the vet.
Bus drivers work here. They drive people where they need to go.
I need a ride across town.
I go to the bus stop.
A bus driver works at the bus stop.
Bus drivers drive people where they need to go.
Farmers work here. They grow food and raise animals.
I want to see where eggs come from.
A farmer works at the farm.
Farmers grow food and raise animals.
